hits.full_text:
If you get addicted to things easily, you have one of the rarest traits there is.

Most people can't stay interested in anything for more than a week. You can lose 6 hours to something without noticing.

Right now that goes to games, feeds, and whatever hooks you first. That's the only problem.

Pick one hard thing actually worth being addicted to. A skill, your body, your work. Give it the same obsession for 2 years and you'll pass people who've been at it for 10.
hits.hook: thedankoe: redirect easy-addiction / 6-hour focus to one hard thing for 2 years (soften into quiet craft, not hustle)
hits.draft_en:
Losing six hours to something isn't rare for me. The feeds already know that.

I'm trying to point the same attention at one hard quiet thing. A craft. A body of work. Something that still looks like progress after two years, not two weeks.

Same wiring. Better target.
hits.video_tip: 16 seconds, morning desk, natural light, room sound. Phone face-down. Hand opens a notebook, writes one short line, closes it. Last frame text: 'Same attention. Quieter target.'

The real secret to looking younger:

Moisturize your face every night.

It's crazy that people will work out, eat clean foods, optimize sleep, and then completely ignore skin health. It's the largest organ in your body and also the most commonly neglected.

That's why I created the Wild Roman Face Moisturizer: … Try it now (10% off)

reply_ideas.reply_text: The rare part isn't getting hooked. It's choosing where it goes. I'm aiming mine at one hard quiet thing for a couple of years — not the first feed that lights up.
Losing six hours without noticing used to feel like a flaw. Lately it feels like unused fuel. Pointing it at the desk instead of the scroll.
Internal competition is still the only scoreboard I can stand. Slightly better than yesterday. No audience required.
This one sat with me. Trying to impress people I don't even like is such an expensive habit. Quieter rooms. Better company. Less performing.
